text:
maria_cs: Hey team — Foxgrove is seeing a big p99 spike on text-generation requests from their prod tenant over the last hour. They report timeouts in their app. I opened a ticket: https://redwood.support/tickets/FG-842. Can SRE help investigate?

dan_support: Thanks Maria. I can take first look. Any repro request IDs or example logs from Foxgrove?

maria_cs: They pasted a couple of request_ids in the ticket: req_x1: 0a3f... and req_x2: 0b7a... Also says it happens when they send batches of ~6 short prompts concurrently.

oliver_sre: Seeing the traces for those req IDs — requests are queued for ~1.1s in our front proxy, then stuck in worker for another 2.4s waiting for GPU slot; backend run time normal. Pattern looks like a burst/backpressure event tied to shared subnet on us-west-2a.

raj_engineer: I pulled tenant routing: Foxgrove is on shared capacity pool 'shared-usw2a-g1'. There's another tenant (tent_nova) with high embed throughput currently. Tent_nova shows sustained concurrency and large sequence lengths. Could be noisy neighbor.

infra-bot: autoscaler: pool shared-usw2a-g1 usage = 92% (GPU vram 88%, queued requests 42), scale-actions suppressed due to reserve rules.

oliver_sre: Confirmed noisy neighbor behavior. p95 still OK but p99 jumps during Nova bursts. We have rate-limiter kicking in per-tenant but reservation rules are leaky here because Foxgrove has no reservation and is lower tier.

maria_cs: Foxgrove is asking for a short-term mitigation — they want something low friction (allowlist, reservation, or bypass). They mentioned they can accept slight cost increase.

dan_support: Proposed immediate options to customer: 1) temporary reservation (30d) for dedicated slots, 2) tenant-level allowlist to skip shared queue and use burst pool, 3) instruct app to reduce concurrency or pin model variant. Which do we recommend?

raj_engineer: For quick mitigation: issue a temporary reservation for 4 concurrent slots (small) or add them to the 'burst-exempt' allowlist to route around noisy queue. Reservation is safer long-term, allowlist is quicker. Both require billing approval.

oliver_sre: I can do a one-off allowlist route for Foxgrove that routes requests to spare burst capacity for next 48h. Will monitor. Need customer tenant_id and contact.

maria_cs: Tenant id: tenant_fox_007. Contact is @foxgrove_prod_owner. Customer accepts allowlist for 48h + we will evaluate reservation. Please proceed.

infra-bot: routing-service: allowlist applied -> tenant_fox_007 routed to burst-exempt queue (us-west-2a) at 2024-07-05T15:34:22Z.

oliver_sre: Applied. Can someone ask customer to repro and share a fresh req_id if latency persists?

foxgrove_prod_owner: Thanks — running a few smoke tests now. First run: req_fox_aa123 -> p99 reduced from ~3.5s to 0.36s. Great. Running more.

maria_cs: Customer confirmed improvement. They're happy with short-term fix but want an ops path to avoid recurring incidents.

raj_engineer: Next steps for product/infra: 1) propose a small reservation SKU for customers like Foxgrove (4-8 concurrency) priced for short-term commits, 2) tighten autoscaler thresholds to allow faster bursting when queues spike, 3) expand observability per-tenant for concurrent model sequence length spikes.

oliver_sre: Also recommending we add a protective heuristic: if a tenant generates >X long-seq embed requests for Y minutes, throttle them more aggressively or move to separate pool automatically. Will draft RFC.

dan_support: I'll coordinate billing approval for the temporary reservation option if they want it after 48h.

maria_cs: Noted. I'll follow up with Foxgrove on commit preference.

oliver_sre: Follow-up action items assigned: oliver_sre -> monitor allowlist and collect p99 metrics (48h), raj_engineer -> draft SKU + autoscaler tweak PR, maria_cs -> confirm with customer on reservation decision, dan_support -> ensure billing flow available.

foxgrove_prod_owner: Appreciate quick help — will provide any logs if we hit anything odd during the test window.

maria_cs: Closing loop here: please keep this thread updated. If p99 climbs again we may move to a dedicated reservation. :thumbsup:
